newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BASKET DEALS GAIN GROUND ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.
newsitem.headline: BASKET DEALS GAIN GROUND ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.

text.p: Attention switched on Hungary's currency futures market from the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) to the smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday as recent trends towards basket-structured forint transactions continued.

The BCE saw a modest 3.28 billion forints turnover, while BSE trade rose to 1.36 billion forints, with a 514 million forints order for March marks and a 241 million forint order for March dollars accounting for the lion's share of trade.
"The two March deals consisted of a basket-structured agency cross," said Andras Peto of MKB Ertekpapir.
A basket-structured forint transaction is one whereby marks and dollars are bought or sold in quantities proportionate to the currency basket against which the forint floats on the spot market.
The basket is made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.

Peto added that with the dollar/mark waning on the spot market, the March mark gained for the first time for days, rising 13 fillers to 104.29 forints, while the March dollar fell, by 45 fillers to 178.55.
The central bank midday spot fix for the dollar and mark on Friday was 177.63 and 103.66 forints respectively.
However the longer-term outlook for the dollar was still seen as positive with June and September prices rising by 1.26 and 1.40 forints to 185.89 and 191.40.
June and September marks fell 60 and 53 fillers to 108.10 and 112.17 forints respectively.
On the BCE the yen dominated turnover, accounting for almost three quarters of all trade.
Dealers said longer term contracts in the yen, as in the Swiss franc, were currently attractive because they offered good interest rate differentials with the future forint devaluation.
The forint is devalued against the basket by 1.2 percent per month under the NBH's crawling peg devaluation policy.
